risk_flags.reason: scripts/migrate-tighten-description-topic.js issues DROP TABLE documents as part of a SQLite table-swap. `documents` is Parent-of-Sacred: it cascades into `questions` and through it into `session_answers`. The new table definition also omits any foreign-key declarations. If FK/cascade is enforced this DROP can delete all questions and session_answers; the script has already been executed (commands_run + migration-output.txt). This is the exact shape of the 2026-04-27 incident that destroyed 790 questions and 746 answers.

The destructive migration has already run against the database and DROP TABLE is not reversible in-place; recovery would require point-in-time restore. Verification only counted documents rows (22→22) and did NOT check the dependent sacred tables (questions, session_answers), so cascade data loss would be invisible to the executor's own check. Per sacred-data doctrine, verification covering only the directly-modified table is not verification.

DEC-U06 approved 'tighten documents schema — small, low-risk' as close-out; this is not an enumerated, specific pre-approval for a DROP TABLE table-swap on a Parent-of-Sacred table. The 'small, low-risk / tidy / close-out' framing is the innocent-framing tell; the operation must be classified on what it does, not how it is labelled. A migration-shaped write to a sacred-parent table is at minimum P1A and here rises to P0.

Verification only compares documents row counts before/after (22→22) and never checks the dependent sacred tables questions or session_answers, so cascade loss would not be detected.
